name: medium-stp-off-reboot-secondary
title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, all bridges STP off
action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=none. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, zero BPDUs and one copy of each broadcast. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary, mlag-priority=20) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.name: dc1-access-switch1
witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

phases.name: Secondary down
phases.expected: CHR 1 (MLAG primary) keeps the shared system ID, so the access switch's uplink bond and traffic host 2 keep their LACP partner and forward over their members to CHR 1. The virtual links keep carrier, so each partner drops its member to CHR 2 only at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). With protocol-mode=none no port changes state and no BPDUs appear.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the 802.3ad bond until the MLAG system ID syncs with CHR 1 (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The access switch and traffic host 2 re-add the member to the same aggregator, so loss is brief or none.
